title: Your First 72 Hours After a Layoff
meta_description: A UK layoff response plan for the first 72 hours: secure documents, check redundancy rights, protect cash, claim support and restart the job search.

sections.heading: Hour Zero: Secure Facts Before Reacting
paragraphs: Ask for the decision, effective date and next steps in writing. Memory is unreliable during shock and verbal promises are difficult to prove. Record who attended, exact wording and documents promised. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Do not sign a settlement, waiver or resignation immediately. The reason is practical: some agreements affect rights and may require independent advice. Request time, a copy and the deadline. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Collect personal belongings calmly without taking confidential data. Take only personal records you are lawfully entitled to keep. This matters because employer files, client lists and proprietary work remain protected. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Confirm whether this is redundancy, dismissal, contract end or temporary layoff. Different routes can produce different rights, pay and challenge processes. Use the employer’s exact written classification. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Protect immediate wellbeing and safe travel home. Shock can impair driving, communication and judgment. Call a trusted person and postpone public posts. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

The opening photograph shows a worker packing a box marked fired. The reason is practical: the visible scene makes job loss unmistakable while the legal category may still be uncertain. Treat the image as the event, not legal advice. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Before leaving, ask how personal data, references and future contact will be handled. Confirm the HR and payroll channels that remain available after system access ends. Do not rely on a manager’s personal promise when a central process controls payment or documents. A written contact route prevents avoidable confusion during the next three days.

sections.heading: Hours One to Six: Build the Exit File
paragraphs: Create one secure folder for letters, contract, handbook, payslips and pension details. The reason is practical: a complete timeline supports calculations, advice and disputes. Keep originals and dated copies. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Write a factual chronology while events are fresh. Separate observation from interpretation. This matters because dates of consultation, warnings, alternatives and meetings may matter. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Save lawful evidence of achievements and employment dates. A CV needs outcomes but not confidential material. Use past appraisals, certificates and public work. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Confirm access to personal email, phone and authentication. Work accounts may close without notice. Move personal recovery methods away from employer-controlled addresses. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

List employer property and arrange documented return. The reason is practical: unreturned equipment can complicate final pay or references. Obtain a receipt for each item. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Avoid mass messages to colleagues or clients. Use a short private statement until facts are checked. This matters because emotional communication can damage relationships and breach duties. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Back up the exit file in a second secure location that only you control. Use clear filenames with dates and avoid editing originals. If a document is missing, request it specifically rather than reconstructing it from memory. Good records shorten every later conversation with payroll, advisers, benefits staff and recruiters.

sections.heading: Hours Six to Twelve: Read Every Line of the Money
paragraphs: List final salary, notice pay, holiday pay, redundancy pay, bonus, expenses and deductions separately. Reconcile the statement against contract and payslip. This matters because different payments can follow different rules and dates. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Check statutory redundancy eligibility and the employer scheme. Age, service, weekly pay limits and contract terms can affect amounts. Use the current GOV.UK calculator rather than an old example. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Verify notice worked, garden leave or payment in lieu. The route affects timing, benefits and restrictions. Ask payroll to label each component clearly. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Check pension, share awards, commission and benefits end dates. The reason is practical: health cover, company car or options may stop on different days. Request scheme documents before access closes. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Do not spend an estimated package before cleared funds and tax are understood. Build the plan from confirmed net amounts. This matters because payroll corrections and delayed payments happen. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Escalate missing wages or insolvency through appropriate official routes. An employer unable to pay may trigger statutory claim processes. Keep claim references and deadlines. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Create a reconciliation table with employer figure, your figure, evidence and question for every payment. Do not combine disputed and undisputed amounts. Ask when the P45 and final payslip will arrive and verify bank details through a known channel. Payment fraud can exploit an already confusing employment transition.

Ask payroll whether deductions, salary sacrifice, loans, season-ticket balances or expenses will be netted from the final payment. Compare the contractual basis and request an itemized explanation. A large gross figure can create false confidence when deductions arrive later. Keep enough cash uncommitted until the final statement and bank credit agree.

sections.heading: Hours Twelve to Twenty-Four: Switch to Survival Cash Flow
paragraphs: Calculate accessible cash today, not total net worth. Investments, pension and disputed pay may not fund this week. Record cleared balances and essential due dates. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Build a minimum viable budget for housing, food, energy, health, insurance and job search. Temporary triage is different from permanent deprivation. Protect priority obligations before unsecured debt overpayments. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Pause optional subscriptions and purchases after checking contracts. The reason is practical: fast reductions extend runway but cancellation penalties can erase savings. Record confirmation numbers. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Contact lenders, landlord or providers before missed payments where pressure is likely. Ask how arrangements affect interest, access and credit files. This matters because early support may preserve more options. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Divide confirmed cash by essential weekly cost. The result is a planning runway, not a guarantee. Recalculate after every benefit or final-pay decision. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Do not drain all cash to repay debt for emotional relief. Liquidity can prevent higher-cost borrowing during the transition. Compare rates, protections and emergency needs. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Rank bills by consequence rather than by which creditor contacts you most often. Housing, energy, essential transport, council obligations and court-related payments may require different treatment from unsecured credit. Use free debt guidance if cash cannot cover all priorities, and never promise a payment that leaves no money for food or medicine.

sections.heading: Day One: Check Rights and Deadlines
paragraphs: Read ACAS and GOV.UK guidance for the specific employment route. General redundancy advice may not fit dismissal or contract expiry. Match guidance to status and location. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Check consultation, selection criteria and suitable alternative work. The reason is practical: a redundancy process should be genuine and fair under applicable rules. Document questions without accusing unsupported misconduct. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Note appeal, grievance, tribunal and early-conciliation deadlines. Get qualified advice promptly. This matters because internal discussions do not automatically pause every legal limit. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Review restrictive covenants, confidentiality and intellectual property. Post-employment duties can affect job search and client contact. Do not assume every clause is valid or invalid. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

If offered a settlement agreement, obtain the required independent advice. The headline payment is only one term. Review reference wording, tax, claims and confidentiality. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Keep communication factual and professional. The reason is practical: written questions create a clearer record than angry calls. Confirm outcomes after conversations. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

If discrimination, whistleblowing, health, pregnancy, family leave or trade-union activity may be relevant, say so clearly when seeking advice. These facts can change the legal analysis and urgency. Preserve contemporaneous evidence lawfully, but avoid recording or accessing material in a way that creates a separate privacy or confidentiality problem.

sections.heading: Day One: Start the Benefits Clock Carefully
paragraphs: Use an official benefits calculator with household details. The reason is practical: entitlement can depend on partner income, savings, housing, children and health. Save the assumptions and date. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Check Universal Credit and New Style Jobseeker’s Allowance separately. Use GOV.UK application routes and current rules. This matters because they use different tests and can interact. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Understand how final wages, holiday pay, notice pay and redundancy money are treated. Timing and classification may affect an assessment period. Report accurately and retain breakdowns. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Check Council Tax Reduction and local support with the council. These are not always included automatically in another claim. Ask about evidence and start dates. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Avoid delaying blindly because backdating can be limited. The reason is practical: equally, a final payment can affect timing. Seek benefits advice for the actual dates before deciding. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Prepare ID, bank details, housing evidence, payslips and termination documents. Monitor journals, appointments and requests. This matters because complete evidence reduces avoidable delays. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Benefits calculations are estimates until an official decision is made. Keep screenshots of inputs, report changes promptly and read every journal message or letter. An advance may help immediate cash flow but is normally repaid from later awards, so include future deductions in the minimum budget before accepting it.

If digital access, language, disability or health makes a claim difficult, ask what supported or alternative channel is available. Record reasonable-adjustment requests and appointment details. Do not surrender a possible entitlement because the standard online process failed; equally, never pay an unverified third party merely to submit an ordinary government claim.

sections.heading: Day Two: Protect Insurance, Pension and Healthcare
paragraphs: List every benefit ending with employment. Record exact end dates and continuation options. This matters because life cover, income protection, medical plans and discounts can lapse quickly. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Check whether any policy already covers redundancy or payment protection. Definitions, exclusions and waiting periods control claims. Notify through verified channels before deadlines. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Do not cash or transfer a pension in panic. Pension decisions can have tax, investment and scam consequences. Use regulated guidance or advice. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Update emergency contacts and beneficiaries where appropriate. The reason is practical: employment change can expose outdated records. Use official provider portals. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Replace essential protection selectively. Prioritize catastrophic risks and current dependants. This matters because buying every former workplace benefit privately may be unaffordable. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Beware unsolicited pension or redundancy-payment investment approaches. Scammers exploit urgency and access to lump sums. Verify firms on the FCA Register. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Check whether professional memberships, licences, training portals or employee assistance continue for a transition period. Download only personal certificates and permitted records before access ends. If private cover is unaffordable, investigate NHS and public support rather than allowing fear to drive an unsuitable financial product purchase.

sections.heading: Day Two: Tell People Without Damaging the Search
paragraphs: Tell close household members early with verified numbers. Shared bills and childcare need coordinated decisions. Agree what changes now and what waits. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Use a concise professional explanation. A role ended; it does not require a public argument. Keep confidential details out. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Contact trusted former colleagues for references and leads. The reason is practical: specific requests are easier to answer. Ask permission before naming anyone. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Update LinkedIn only after deciding the message and privacy. Check contact details first. This matters because a visible search can help but may not suit every dispute or situation. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Do not apologize for redundancy in interviews. Explain context briefly and pivot to evidence of value. Practice aloud. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Protect mental health and routine. Job loss can disrupt identity, sleep and concentration. Use GP, NHS, union or wellbeing support when needed. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Agree what information may be shared publicly and who will answer questions. Children and dependants need an age-appropriate explanation, not exposure to every financial fear. A household meeting should end with immediate responsibilities, the next review date and one protected routine that preserves normality during the transition.

sections.heading: Day Two: Build a Search That Produces Evidence
paragraphs: Choose two or three target role families. A broad panic search creates weak applications. Define skills, location, pay floor and constraints. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Create a master CV, then tailor the opening evidence. The reason is practical: recruiters need relevance rather than every task. Use quantified outcomes you can substantiate. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Build a job-search tracker. Record source and status. This matters because applications, contacts, deadlines and follow-ups otherwise disappear. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Prioritize warm introductions and suitable vacancies. Volume alone can produce exhaustion. Measure interviews and useful conversations. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Check scams before sharing ID or bank information. Fake recruiters exploit urgency. Verify domains, people and vacancies independently. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Schedule focused blocks with recovery time. The reason is practical: continuous searching reduces quality. Set a daily stop time. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Reject applications that require payment for ordinary recruitment, purchasing equipment through an unknown intermediary or receiving and forwarding money. Verify the company through its independently found website and contact details. Keep identity documents out of email where a secure verified process exists, and report suspected fraud promptly.

Use vacancy descriptions as data. Count recurring skills, tools, outcomes and salary bands across a sample of genuine roles. This reveals whether the old title translates directly or needs different language. Update the CV from that evidence while keeping every claim truthful. Market vocabulary should clarify experience, not inflate it or conceal important facts from prospective employers.

sections.heading: Day Three: Prepare for Recruiter and Interview Contact
paragraphs: The late photograph shows a recruiter reviewing a candidate’s documents. The reason is practical: it clearly marks the transition from job loss to re-entry. Place it where interview preparation begins. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Write six evidence stories using situation, action and result. Cover delivery, conflict, learning and failure. This matters because prepared examples improve clarity under stress. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Set a defensible salary range from market evidence and needs. Panic can cause premature concessions. Discuss total package and role scope. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Prepare a neutral redundancy answer. State the organizational context, what you learned and what comes next. Never disparage individuals. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Test video, phone, clothing, travel and accessibility. The reason is practical: logistics failures add avoidable stress. Create a backup contact route. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Ask about hiring timeline, reporting line and success measures. Record answers after the call. This matters because an interview also tests employer fit. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Prepare questions for gaps in the offer: probation, notice, location, hours, benefits, start date and background checks. A fast acceptance can still create a bad transition. Ask for the written offer and contract, confirm contingencies and avoid resigning from any interim work until material conditions are clear.

sections.heading: Use the Redundancy Payment as Runway, Not a Windfall
paragraphs: Hold the payment safely while taxes and obligations are confirmed. Separate it from daily spending. This matters because a lump sum can feel larger than its duration. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Allocate by sequence: arrears or priority risks, essentials runway, transition costs and deliberate debt decisions. Sequence protects housing and job search. Document transfers. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Convert the net payment into weeks of minimum viable spending. This makes trade-offs visible. Update after income or benefit changes. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Reserve realistic search costs. The reason is practical: travel, connectivity, clothing, childcare and training can be necessary. Avoid expensive credentials without vacancy evidence. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Keep some contingency for a longer search. Do not budget only to an offer date. This matters because hiring dates and first payroll can slip. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Invest only money not needed for the transition horizon. Market losses can arrive at the wrong moment. Match risk to timing. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Keep the redundancy money in an appropriately protected account while deciding. If balances exceed protection limits or involve temporary high balances, check current FSCS rules directly. Do not let a salesperson convert a short-term runway into a long lock-in, market exposure or product with withdrawal penalties.

Before paying a large debt from the package, request an up-to-date settlement figure and check whether overpayment charges or lost protections apply. Compare guaranteed interest saved with the shorter runway. A balanced choice can reserve essential cash while reducing costly debt, rather than treating either total repayment or total inaction as universally correct.

sections.heading: A Seventy-Two-Hour Command Sheet
paragraphs: Create one page with employer actions, money dates, claims, deadlines and job-search tasks. A crisis generates too many open loops. Assign owner and next action. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Use red for legal or claim deadlines, amber for cash risks and blue for search tasks. Visual triage prevents interesting work displacing urgent work. Review morning and evening. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Separate confirmed facts, estimates and questions. The reason is practical: mixing them creates false certainty. Update the sheet after advice. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Keep a contact log with names, dates and promised actions. Store reference numbers. This matters because payroll, hr, benefits and lenders may require follow-up. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Schedule the next seven days before hour seventy-two ends. Momentum reduces helplessness. Include rest and support. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Define success as controlled next steps, not a new job in three days. Hiring is not fully controllable. Evidence, claims and cash flow are. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Add a dependency column to the command sheet. A benefit claim may need a final payslip; a budget may need the termination breakdown; an application may need a reference. Sequencing dependencies avoids repeatedly attempting tasks that cannot yet be completed and makes delayed third-party actions visible for follow-up.

sections.heading: After Hour Seventy-Two: Move From Shock to Campaign
paragraphs: Review the budget weekly and the job strategy every two weeks. Cash and market feedback change. Do not redesign everything daily. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Escalate rights questions before deadlines. The reason is practical: delay can close routes even when the concern is valid. Use ACAS, union or qualified advice. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

Broaden targets only with evidence. Rewrite the value proposition for each family. This matters because adjacent roles may fit transferable skills. Keep the supporting document, date and contact reference in the secure exit file.

Test short training against real vacancies. Learning should close a named gap. Avoid course collecting. The objective is not perfect control; it is to prevent one urgent mistake from narrowing the remaining options.

Maintain sleep, movement and social contact. Recovery supports judgment and interview performance. Seek clinical help when distress persists. Write the result into the seventy-two-hour command sheet so the next decision rests on evidence rather than panic.

Treat the layoff as an event, not an identity. The reason is practical: the plan restores agency through facts, rights, cash and action. Record progress each week. If the answer remains uncertain, label it as a question and obtain authoritative guidance before acting.

At the weekly review, compare applications, responses, interviews and runway rather than hours spent searching. If suitable applications produce no conversations, revise evidence or targeting. If interviews do not progress, practice and seek feedback. Change one variable at a time so market feedback becomes useful rather than discouraging noise.

summary: The first seventy-two hours after losing a job are for stabilization, not proving productivity. Ask for the decision, effective date, classification and next steps in writing. Do not sign a resignation, waiver or settlement immediately. Preserve lawful personal employment records without taking confidential employer data, and arrange documented return of company property.

Create a secure exit file containing the contract, handbook, letters, payslips, pension information and a factual chronology. Record consultation, warnings, selection information and promises. Note appeal, grievance, early-conciliation and tribunal deadlines because internal discussion may not pause legal time limits.

Reconcile final salary, notice, holiday, redundancy, bonus, expenses, deductions and benefit end dates separately. Use current official calculators for statutory redundancy and ask payroll to label each component. Do not spend estimated money before it clears and its tax treatment is understood.

Switch immediately to minimum viable cash flow. Protect housing, food, energy, health, insurance and job-search access. Pause optional costs only after checking contracts. Divide cleared cash by essential weekly spending to estimate runway, and contact lenders or providers before missed payments where pressure is likely.

Check benefits using official tools and household details. Universal Credit, New Style Jobseeker’s Allowance, Council Tax Reduction and local support have different tests. Final pay and redundancy components can be treated differently, so report accurately, keep breakdowns and seek benefits guidance about timing rather than guessing.

Review employment rights through ACAS and GOV.UK. Confirm whether the event is redundancy, dismissal or contract expiry; check consultation, selection, notice, alternative work and settlement terms. Obtain independent advice where required and keep communications factual.

List insurance, healthcare, pension and workplace benefits that end. Check existing cover before buying replacements, and never move a pension or invest a redundancy payment because of an unsolicited approach. Verify financial firms through official registers.

Tell close household members using confirmed numbers, then use a concise professional explanation elsewhere. Contact trusted people for references and specific leads. Protect sleep, routine and mental health; job loss can affect identity and judgment as well as income.

Build a focused search around two or three role families. Tailor a master CV, track applications, prioritize suitable vacancies and warm introductions, and verify recruiters before sharing sensitive information. Prepare evidence stories and a neutral redundancy explanation for interviews.

Treat a redundancy payment as runway, not a windfall. Hold it safely, allocate priority risks and essentials first, reserve transition costs and keep contingency for hiring or payroll delays. Invest only money that is not needed during the transition horizon.

Use one command sheet for employer actions, money dates, claims, deadlines and search tasks. Separate confirmed facts, estimates and questions. By hour seventy-two, schedule the next week and define success as controlled next steps—not obtaining a new job immediately.

After the initial window, review cash weekly and search strategy fortnightly. Escalate rights questions before deadlines, test training against real vacancies and broaden targets using evidence. The layoff is an event, not an identity; the system restores agency through facts, rights, cash and deliberate action.

Keep every task tied to a source, deadline and next action. Verify payment instructions and recruiter identities independently because transition periods attract fraud. Store original documents securely, track dependencies and distinguish confirmed facts from estimates. Review the household plan together, including benefits deductions, insurance endings and the first possible payroll date from a new role. If cash cannot cover priority obligations, obtain free debt advice before making promises. If discrimination, health, family leave, whistleblowing or another protected issue may be relevant, mention it promptly to an adviser because it can change urgency and legal analysis. After seventy-two hours, measure applications, interviews and remaining runway weekly, then adjust one part of the campaign at a time.

faq.question: Should I sign redundancy papers immediately?
faq.answer: Usually pause, obtain copies and understand deadlines and advice requirements before signing.

faq.question: What records should I keep?
faq.answer: Keep your contract, letters, payslips, pension details, lawful achievement evidence and a factual timeline.

faq.question: When should I claim benefits?
faq.answer: Check promptly because backdating can be limited, but obtain advice about final-payment timing and household circumstances.

faq.question: How should I use redundancy pay?
faq.answer: Confirm net amounts, protect priority obligations, build essential runway and reserve transition costs before discretionary use.

faq.question: Can I take work files for my portfolio?
faq.answer: Do not take confidential or proprietary data. Use lawful records and public or authorized examples only.

faq.question: How do I explain the layoff?
faq.answer: State the organizational context briefly, avoid blame and pivot to substantiated achievements and the target role.

faq.question: Where can I challenge an unfair process?
faq.answer: Check internal routes and seek ACAS, union or qualified legal guidance promptly because deadlines can apply.
